title: Calibration job router, shard-aware retention, and accuracy-gating UX
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Implement a router and UX improvements in Redwood Console to improve calibration job placement, artifact retention by shard, and accuracy-gating for promotion of quantization profiles (FP8/INT8). Background: customers run large calibration sweeps across mixed-model fleets; current monolithic retention and a single queue for calibration jobs causes noisy SLOs, long repro times, and manual artifact cleanup. This ticket introduces three coordinated features: 1) Calibration job router: policy-driven placement that routes runs to dedicated executors (small/medium/huge) and autoscaling pools based on model size, seq length distribution, and calibration type (per-tensor vs per-channel). Router must support priority, tenant isolation for Dedicated, and fallback paths. 2) Shard-aware retention: artifacts (calibration traces, quant profiles, eval results) should be recorded with shard fingerprints and retention TTLs per-shard and per-run-type. Support archive-to-cold-tier (S3 Glacier-style) and a lightweight index for quick lookup. 3) Accuracy-gating UX: in Console, provide a clear pass/fail result for runs vs baseline with configurable thresholds (absolute/relative), show per-metric deltas and confidence intervals, and enable a one-click promotion flow to model catalog or rollback to baseline. Deliverables: API changes, Console screens, retention policy enforcement job, and RBAC roles for run viewers, executors, and promotion approvers.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration job router accepts policy config and routes test runs to appropriate executor pools based on model metadata and resource tags.
Shard-aware retention stores artifacts with shard IDs and honors per-shard TTLs; archived artifacts are searchable via Console index within 30s of archive completion.
Console shows accuracy-gating results with pass/fail, metric deltas, and a Promotion button that creates a promotion request or directly promotes when user has 'calib:promote' permission.
Permissions: three new roles documented and enforceable via Private RBAC and Hosted permission sets: calibration.viewer, calibration.executor, calibration.promoter.

E2E tests: an automated calibration sweep creates artifacts, ages them beyond TTL and confirms they are archived/deleted per policy; a promoted profile appears in model catalog with provenance metadata linking to original run and artifacts.
Performance: routing adds <5% median latency to job submission and does not increase overall scheduling failures compared to baseline in dedicated staging cluster.
design_notes: Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/Calib-Job-Router-UX (mock v3). Architecture sketch and PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Calibration+Router+and+Shard+Retention. Key UI decisions: emphasize pass/fail at top, provide an expandable per-metric breakdown, and surface a confidence band for small-sample runs. Use existing rollout modal pattern for promotions to model catalog.
implementation_plan: 1. Schema: add shard_id and retention_ttl to calibration_run and artifact metadata in control plane DB.
2. Router service: implement policy engine (rules: model_size, avg_seq_len, calibration_type, tenant_tier) and integrate with existing scheduler API (ENG-18120).
3. Retention worker: implement archive pipeline to S3 cold-tier and an indexable manifest in hot DB for quick listing.
4. Console: new Calibration Run detail page with accuracy gate summary, per-metric delta table, and Promotion button wired to promotion API.
5. RBAC: add new permission checks in control plane and Console; map to Hosted roles and document Dedicated mapping for enterprise admins.
6. Tests: integration tests for routing correctness, retention TTL enforcement, and promotion workflow with provenance metadata.
7. Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag; enable for internal teams, then opt-in customers, then default on for hosted in 3 weeks.
8. Observability: add routing metrics (route hit, fallback rate), retention job metrics (archive latency, fail rate), and UX telemetry for Promotion clicks and errors.
risks: 1) Storage cost for long-lived per-shard artifacts may grow quickly; mitigation: set sensible default TTLs and throttled archive. 2) Incorrect routing policies could overload small pools; mitigation: circuit-breaker and automatic fallback to general pool. 3) Promotion without sufficient validation may regress quality; mitigation: require promoter permission and optionally an approval flow for high-risk models.
